description.narrative: The proposed project aims to improve the water supply system in the country's capital, Dhaka, by making it more reliable, sustainable, and climate-resilient. It will consolidate and enhance the gains made in the efficiency of the water distribution network achieved under two ongoing Asian Development Bank (ADB) projects, and improve the service delivery and the capacity of the Dhaka Water Supply and Sewerage Authority (DWASA).

description.narrative: Output/s as listed by the project staff.

Output: Capacity for quality service delivery enhanced. Indicator: 35 CBOs organized and implemented in LICs Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Achieved. 42 CBOs (18 new CBOs + 24 existing CBOs in LIC areas) are formed. Training/orientation for 19 CBOs committee will be conducted by 2025. Combinedly in existing and newly formed CBOs; committees comprised of total 355 members including 215 women (60.56%), 211 members are in leadership position including 109 women (51.66%). In case of newly formed CBOs, 81 members are in leadership position, including 43 women (53.08%). Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR

Output: Capacity for quality service delivery enhanced. Indicator: 50 DWASA staff, trained for operationalizing laboratory Achievement: 52 Progress/Status: Installation of laboratory equipment is completed. Till date, 52 staff are trained including 10 eligible (100%) women staff. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR

Output: Capacity for quality service delivery enhanced. Indicator: by Q1 2020, with women making up at least 50% of all participants and filling 50% of leadership positions Achievement: 113.68 Progress/Status: Achieved. Of the CBOs organized, about 60.6% are women members, and 53.08% of the leadership position are held by women. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR

Output: Capacity for quality service delivery enhanced. Indicator: with 100% eligible women staff as training participants Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: All eligible 10 women staff (100%) are trained. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR

Output: Distribution network strengthened. Indicator: (i) 1,500 kilometers of water distribution network rehabilitated Achievement: 562 Progress/Status: Achieved. 2,546 km of water distribution network rehabilitated. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys, QPRs, and PCR

Output: Distribution network strengthened. Indicator: (ii) 187,000 connections to households and communities rehabilitated, from which at least 2.4 million women will benefit Achievement: 63466 Progress/Status: 203,150 household and community connections rehabilitated, including 198,075 replaced meters, benefitting about 2.56 million women. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys, QPRs, and PCR

Output: Distribution network strengthened. Indicator: (iii) 34,000 new or legalized connections of households and communities, from which at least 425,000 women will benefit Achievement: 11815 Progress/Status: 34,174 new or legalized household and community connections installed benefitting about 517,282 women. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys, QPRs, and PCR

Output: Distribution network strengthened. Indicator: (iv) 4,500 new or legalized connections of LICs, from which at least 125,000 women will benefit Achievement: 2817 Progress/Status: 4,845 new or legalized connections to LICs provided, benefitting about 137,454 women. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys, QPRs, and PCR

Output: Sustainable managerial capacity of DMA enhanced. Indicator: i. with 100% eligible women staff as training participants Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: All 11 eligible women staff (100%) have been participated in the training. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR

Output: Capacity for quality service delivery enhanced. Indicator: Awareness campaign program implemented in seven zones by 2024 Achievement: 1873512 Progress/Status: Achieved. Awareness campaign program ongoing in 7 zones. • In community consultation meetings, total number of participants were 1,873,512 including 946,747 (50.53%) women participants. • 1,929 consultation sessions (390 Public consultations, 745 FGDs and 794 tea stall meetings) have been conducted. Total number of participants were 37,770 including 12,862 (34.05%) women participants.
Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR

Output: Capacity for quality service delivery enhanced. Indicator: with women making up at least 30% of participants Achievement: 50.53 Progress/Status: Achieved. Of the awareness campaign program arranged, • In community consultation meetings, about 50.53% of the participants were women. • In consultation sessions, about 34.05% of the participants were women. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR

Output: Capacity for quality service delivery enhanced. Indicator: Bidding documents for two future investment projects ready by 2025 Progress/Status: Ongoing. The Project Steering Committee (PSC) recommended discontinuation of the Land Acquisition Project. Consequently, Dhaka WASA Management has decided to relocate the proposed Sewage Treatment Plant (STP) site to Pagla, utilizing DWASA's own land for this purpose. Moreover, the proposal for utilizing the existing DSIP Pagla Eastern Trunk Main (from Gandaria Junction point to Pagla STP) until completion of the construction works under DSIP Phase-3 has also been approved by Dhaka WASA Management. The variation of the PDF Consultant has been approved. Revised contract has been signed and Consultant DOHWA (JV Lead) commenced their work as per revised ToR. Since the DWSNIP Project is scheduled to close in December 2025, the Project Steering Committee (PSC) has recommended transferring this PDF Consultant Package to the DESWSP Project for continuation of remaining activities Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Capacity for quality service delivery enhanced. Indicator: Five-year corporate business plan improved and implemented in 2025 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. The upgraded 5-Yr Corporate Business Plan is finalized, approved, and now in implementation. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Capacity for quality service delivery enhanced. Indicator: Gender action plan implemented by 2025 Progress/Status: Achieved. As per the Gender Action Plan (GAP), a total of 18 targets were identified. All these targets were successfully achieved by 31 December 2025 Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Capacity for quality service delivery enhanced. Indicator: Water quality monitoring system upgraded and implemented by 2025 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. Water quality monitoring equipment are already installed by the supplier and being used in DWASA Laboratories. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Distribution network strengthened. Indicator: In new DMAs, covered by the project Progress/Status: Achieved. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys, QPRs, and PCR Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Distribution network strengthened. Indicator: Output e1 of the design and monitoring framework for the Dhaka Water Supply Sector Development Program Accomplished Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. All remaining works of DWSSDP completed. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys, QPRs, and PCR Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2017 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Sustainable managerial capacity of DMA enhanced. Indicator: 700 Dhaka WASA staff (seven zones) trained in DMA management by 2025 Achievement: 847 Progress/Status: Achieved. To date, 847 DWASA staff have been trained for DMA management. All 11 eligible women staff (100%) have been participated in the training. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: 700 Actual value: 847

Output: Sustainable managerial capacity of DMA enhanced. Indicator: AMR implemented in three model DMAs Progress/Status: 1 package for AMR implementation is under bidding document preparation stage. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Sustainable managerial capacity of DMA enhanced. Indicator: SCADA system implemented in all DMAs by 2025 Progress/Status: Hardware installation works of IWOC and 10 nos Zonal SCADAs are completed. Installation work of SCADA system at 450 new DTWs are completed. Integration and commissioning of all SCADA components are in progress. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y

Output: Sustainable managerial capacity of DMA enhanced. Indicator: SOP upgraded and implemented in 2025 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. 19 nos. of SOP prepared by CBS and training on these SOPs were given to DMA Management and implementation is in progress. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Sustainable managerial capacity of DMA enhanced. Indicator: Sustainable nonrevenue water reduction plan implemented in 2025 Achievement: Y Progress/Status: Achieved. Sustainable DMA Management Tools (SDMT) has been developed, and implementation is in progress including calculation of NRW. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2015 Baseline value: N Target year: 2025 Target value: Y Actual value: Y
Sustainable provision of a more reliable, improved, and climate-resilient supply of water ensured in Dhaka City

Water supply pressure of at least 1 bar (10 meters) at consumer end achieved (2015 baseline: 0.1-0.5 bar) Achievement: 1 Progress/Status: Water tightness tests conducted in each DMA have confirmed that the DMA pipelines can sustain a minimum pressure of 6 bar. Dhaka WASA is currently maintaining pressure between 2 - 4 bar in those DMAs connected to the Padma transmission line. A minimum pressure of 1 bar has been achieved in most DMAs; however, DWASA cannot yet maintain this level consistently due to source limitations. The situation is expected to improve and stabilize once the source capacity is enhanced. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR

Nonrevenue water reduced to below 10 % (2013-2014 baseline: 26%) Achievement: 5.8 Progress/Status: In commissioned DMAs, NRW measured at a range between 1.6 - 5.8%. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR

98% of water quality test results within DWASA distribution systems meet country standards (2013 baseline: 90%) Achievement: 100 Progress/Status: In handed over DMAs, 100% test results met country standards. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR

Uninterrupted, 24-hour supply of piped water delivered to 6.5 million people (2015 baseline: intermittent and insufficient supply, 8-10 hours average per day) Achievement: Y Progress/Status: 76 out of 85 DMAs handed over, providing 24/7 piped water supply to 5.60 million population including of LIC households. Data Source: DWASA's annual monitoring surveys QPRs and PCR Base year: 2015 Baseline value: N
